name: Oracle Clinical AI Agent
description: Oracle Clinical AI Agent is Oracle Health's (formerly Cerner) ambient AI scribe integrated into their EHR platform. Launched US early 2025, UK NHS February 2026 after pilots at Barts Health, Imperial College Healthcare, and Milton Keynes. Claims 400,000+ hours of documentation time saved. August 2026 expansion added automated professional fee coding, clinician-controlled dictation, and AI-assisted chart review. Pricing is enterprise-custom only—not publicly available—estimated $400-800+/provider/month based on comparable enterprise solutions. Multi-year contracts required. Contact Oracle Health account representative for availability and pricing.

faqs.q: How much does Oracle Clinical AI Agent cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Oracle does not publish pricing for Clinical AI Agent. It's sold through enterprise contracts that require contacting Oracle Health account representatives. Based on comparable enterprise solutions (Microsoft DAX $400-830/mo), expect premium pricing in the $400-800+/provider/month range with multi-year contracts.

faqs.q: What EHR does Oracle Clinical AI Agent integrate with?
faqs.a: Oracle Clinical AI Agent is native to Oracle Health (formerly Cerner) EHR. It's designed specifically for Oracle Health customers and won't work with Epic, athenahealth, or other EHR platforms.

faqs.q: What new features were added in August 2026?
faqs.a: Oracle Health added automated professional fee coding, clinician-controlled dictation, and AI-assisted chart review in August 2026. These expand beyond pure ambient scribing into coding and pre-visit workflows.

faqs.q: Is Oracle Clinical AI Agent available in the UK?
faqs.a: Yes. Oracle Clinical AI Agent launched for NHS organizations in February 2026 after successful pilots at Barts Health, Imperial College Healthcare, and Milton Keynes University Hospital.

faqs.q: Oracle Clinical AI Agent vs Nuance DAX: which is better for Cerner users?
faqs.a: Oracle Clinical AI Agent is native to Oracle Health (Cerner). Nuance DAX Copilot also integrates with Cerner and has deeper Microsoft backing. Both require enterprise contracts. Contact both Oracle Health and Microsoft for comparative pricing and capabilities.
